title: Pager scrub & SLO review — morning prep
content:
Purpose: quick morning scrub before the SRE weekly ops sync (0900 PT). Goal is to highlight current SLO pressure, recent paging trends, top incidents to call out, and concrete follow-ups for the week.

Attendees (intended): oncall primary, oncall secondary, SRE lead (Asha), infra eng (Diego), platform observability (Linnea)

1) High-level summary
- Overall: small uptick in paging vs last week driven by cache/regression in prefix cache eviction; latency SLOs trending near threshold for serving-runtime for long sequences. No active Sev1s as of 06:30 PT.
- Immediate ask for ops sync: confirm mitigation plan for cache storms, agree owners and timeline for corrective work, and set temporary routing policy to reduce customer impact.

2) SLO snapshot (rolling 7-day, evaluated 2026-03-16 06:00 PT)
- API availability (global): target 99.95% -> current 99.96% (ok, small headroom)
- Inference request tail latency (serving-runtime) p99 target 800ms -> current 880ms (7-day burn 4.6%)
- Token-generation throughput SLO (Dedicated pools): target 95% of reserved throughput -> current 93.2% (bursty nights)
- Embeddings vector API error rate target 0.5% -> current 0.74% (mainly retries / downstream KV miss)

Quick interpretation: main pressure is p99 latency on serving-runtime and embeddings error rate. Availability is fine. Latency likely tied to cache behavior and occasional hot-shard contention.

3) Paging trends (last 7 days vs prior 7 days) — raw page counts per service
- cache-layer: 47 pages (↑ +62% week-over-week). Most pages 03/12–03/14 during rollout of model-quantization-job RWI-1302.
- serving-runtime: 18 pages (↓ -22%). Pages mostly for elevated p99s during long-sequence evals.
- auth-service: 34 pages (↑ +10%). Mostly token refresh failures tied to a flaky KMS integration in one region.
- infra-network: 6 pages (flat)
- routing/proxy: 9 pages (↑ +125% — correlated with cache storms causing circuit-breaker trips)

Notes: cache-layer spike correlates to multiple jobs that invalidated prefixes simultaneously and a bad backoff in the eviction controller.

4) Top incidents (past 7d) — short briefs
- RWI-1327: cache eviction storm (03/13 01:12–02:05 PT) — symptoms: 500s on embeddings endpoint, large KV miss rate, circuit-breaker trips. Mitigation: rolled back quantization job and applied temporary rate-limit to invalidation API. Owner: Diego. Post-mortem started (linked).
- RWI-1302: model-quantization canary caused higher-than-expected memory churn on a subset of Dedicated nodes (03/11). Mitigation: paused rollout, reverted canary. Follow-up: add memory guardrails in compilation stage. Owner: Model infra team — cf. PR #4512.
- RWI-1299: KMS timeout in eu-west-1 (03/14) causing burst of auth errors. Short TTLs and retry storms. Mitigation: increased client-side backoff, engaged KMS vendor. Owner: Security infra (Linnea).

5) Hypotheses and quick evidence to bring to sync
- Hypothesis A: eviction-controller backoff is linear instead of exponential -> simultaneous invalidations cause thundering herd. Evidence: eviction logs show uniform retry delay of 5s. Next step: confirm code path + roll a patch (short-term).
- Hypothesis B: long-sequence latency is amplified by missing KV prefixes for a subset of models -> increased KV lookups + cold cache misses. Evidence to fetch: p99 by model id, cache hit rate pre/post cold-start.

6) Proposed immediate mitigations (vote for 1–2 during sync)
- Add temporary per-tenant invalidation rate limit at edge (low risk) — owner: Diego — ETA 24h
- Increase eviction backoff to exponential in controller (medium risk) — owner: Diego + infra — ETA 48h for patch + canary
- Short-term routing rule: route long-sequence traffic to a larger pool with pinned KV to reduce p99 (ops config change) — owner: SRE lead (Asha) + platform — ETA 6h

7) Action items (concrete)
- Diego: attach eviction-controller logs and current retry config to RWI-1327, create patch branch for exponential backoff, due 2026-03-17.
- Linnea: follow up with KMS vendor for root cause + write proposal for client-side retry strategy changes, due 2026-03-18.
- Asha: draft temporary routing rule config and run tabletop to validate impact on throughput/cost, due 2026-03-16 EOD.
- Observability (Linnea/Diego): add p99-by-model dashboard for serving-runtime (7d/30d) and surface it in the ops console, due 2026-03-20.
- Oncall secondary: monitor pages overnight and escalate if page rate for cache-layer > 60 (threshold), owner: oncall secondary — ongoing.

8) Open questions for product/infra
- Product: is there an expected increase in long-sequence evals this week (batch jobs)? If yes, can we postpone or throttle?
- Infra: can compilation stage add a soft memory cap to fail fast before node-level OOM?

9) Prep notes for the sync agenda (what I will present)
- 5m: quick SLO snapshot + trend chart (p99 / error rate / availability)
- 10m: incidents recap (RWI-1327 and RWI-1302) and current mitigations
- 10m: proposed mitigations + tradeoffs (routing vs eviction patch vs rate limits)
- 5m: action items alignment + owners and deadlines

Quick wins to suggest in meeting: pause non-critical invalidation jobs, add temporary rate limit at ingress, enable per-tenant circuit-breaker thresholds for embeddings.

Notes-to-self: be ready to show logs for eviction burst (filter: eviction_controller.retry_delay_ms), have p99-by-model gif chart handy (slides).

Follow-up plan: after sync, send a short summary thread to #oncall-ops, update RWI-1327 with chosen mitigation and owners, and schedule 30-min postmortem kickoff if rollback/more than 30m customer impact.

— end of prep notes —
summary: Morning prep for SRE ops sync focused on cache eviction storms, serving-runtime p99 pressure, and concrete mitigations with owners and deadlines.
